summary: This defines a RobotPet class whose battery level is guarded by a property setter, so any value assigned to it is clamped into the range 0 to 100. Because the setter runs even during __init__, a pet can never be created or charged into an impossible battery level.

lines.text: This looks like a plain assignment, but because `battery` is a property it calls the setter below, so the clamping rules apply from the moment the pet is created.
The `@property` decorator turns the following method into a read-only attribute, so callers write `pet.battery` rather than `pet.battery()`.
The real value lives in `_battery`, and the leading underscore signals that outside code should go through the property instead of touching it directly.
This registers the next method as the code that runs whenever something assigns to `battery`, which is where the protection is enforced.
Anything below empty is treated as empty rather than rejected, so a large drain simply flattens the battery.
The upper guard means overcharging is harmless: the level stops at a full 100.
Only a value already inside the valid range is stored unchanged.
Charging is written as a simple `+=` because the setter does all the range checking, so this method never needs its own limits.

lines.code: return f"{self.name} performs a generic trick!"
lines.text: Returning the string instead of printing it makes the behaviour easy to assert on in a unit test.
